# Bibliography — goal-5 aggregate/v2 performance research

Read 2026-10-31. Source pin, source-code evidence, documentation, upstream report, and research claims are deliberately distinguished. No source's measurements are measurements of this project. All links below are source references, not requested actions.

## Pinned official DuckDB source

All D1–D6 code is from exact commit `d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa` (project DuckDB 2.0.0 pin), fetched read-only through GitHub.

- **D1 — public v2 declarations:** [`src/include/duckdb_v2.h`](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_v2.h). The manifest records the actually returned connector blob identifier. Relevant modules/lines: function properties 673–779; arena 790–827; column data collection 1191–1538; data-chunk copy 2253–2275; factory 2641–2722; query metrics 4411–4667; aggregate 4890–5888; scalar 10314–10932; vectors 11253–11872. Supports exact public names, callback state/row/offset ownership, properties, views, collection lifecycle, and supported-negative surface inventory. The aggregate module contains 45 exported v2 aggregate-related functions.
- **D2 — extension ABI surface:** [`src/include/duckdb_extension_v2.h`](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_extension_v2.h). Lines 14–78 establish instability, no mixed v1/v2 extension headers, family-2 selection, and unstable opt-in. Pointer table/macros include the actual aggregate, vector, arena, and collection functions.
- **D3 — aggregate bridge implementation:** [`src/main/capi/v2/capi_v2_func_aggregate.cpp`](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/main/capi/v2/capi_v2_func_aggregate.cpp). Lines 160–312: bind, size/init/update/combine/finalize/destroy bridges and error slots; 322–377: required callback validation, signature/return-type checks, properties and callbacks installed on the internal function; 752–796: registration/destruction. Internal implementation is evidence, not a new application dependency.
- **D4 — upstream aggregate test source:** [`test/api/capi/v2/test_capi_v2_aggregate_function.cpp`](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/test/api/capi/v2/test_capi_v2_aggregate_function.cpp). Lines 68–149: representative size/init/update/combine/finalize callbacks; 425–495: grouped, constant, ordered/window and bind-data source cases. Tests were read, not run. Toy unchecked sum code is not a checked-arithmetic implementation proposal.
- **D5 — actual state-spill limitations:** [`src/execution/aggregate_state_spilling.cpp`](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/execution/aggregate_state_spilling.cpp), lines 14–75, especially state-description/destructor gating at 40–69; [`src/execution/radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp`](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/execution/radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp), state-spill setup around 134 and retained-state memory reservation around 873–892; [`src/include/duckdb/function/aggregate_state_serialization.hpp`](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb/function/aggregate_state_serialization.hpp). Compare to D3's v2 builder: public v2 does not install/export these internal state-layout hooks.
- **D6 — built-in sum type and order properties:** [`extension/core_functions/aggregate/distributive/sum.cpp`](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/extension/core_functions/aggregate/distributive/sum.cpp), lines 405–449, specifically BIGINT→HUGEINT at 433–440; DOUBLE aggregate at 557–560. This is why a final BIGINT cast is not an ordered checked-i64-prefix oracle.

## Official documentation and current upstream report

- **D7 — DuckDB 2.0 aggregate semantics:** [Aggregate Functions](https://duckdb.org/docs/2.0/sql/functions/aggregates). NULL/empty-group handling; DISTINCT-by-value; order-sensitive floating-point sum; count versus count(arg). [Numeric Types](https://duckdb.org/docs/2.0/sql/data_types/numeric) is secondary context for SQL type/range adapters; its policies do not expand the Datalog type domain. [C API overview](https://www.duckdb.org/docs/preview/clients/c/overview) distinguishes the unstable v2 headers from v1.
- **D8 — upstream report, not local reproduction:** [DuckDB issue 28132: same-signature C API v2 aggregates returning the first aggregate's result](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/issues/28132). Opened 2026-10-30; labeled reproduced when read on 2026-10-31. Reports two distinct named/callback aggregates in one SELECT and GROUP BY producing the first result twice. The exact pinned project's runtime status is UNRUN. No issue attachment was downloaded and no suggested reproduction/build command was executed.
- **D9 — historical implementation explanation:** [Parallel Grouped Aggregation in DuckDB](https://www.duckdb.org/2022/03/07/aggregate-hashtable), Hannes Mühleisen, 2022-03-07. Two-part storage, cached hashes, hash-prefix filtering, and partitioned merging are architectural background only; old thresholds and performance results were not adopted.

## Primary research

- **R1 — vectorized execution:** Peter Boncz, Marcin Zukowski, Niels Nes. *MonetDB/X100: Hyper-Pipelining Query Execution*. CIDR 2005, pp. 225–237. [Publisher/conference PDF](https://www.cidrdb.org/cidr2005/papers/P19.pdf). In particular section 5.1.1 explains the batch-size/working-set tradeoff. Used only for bounded-vector execution hypotheses; no numerical result is adopted.
- **R2 — parallel grouped aggregation:** Viktor Leis, Peter Boncz, Alfons Kemper, Thomas Neumann. *Morsel-Driven Parallelism: A NUMA-Aware Query Evaluation Framework for the Many-Core Age*. SIGMOD 2014, pp. 743–754. [Author-hosted paper](https://db.in.tum.de/~leis/papers/morsels.pdf). Section 4.4 describes local preaggregation and partition-wise reduction after input completion. Used only for algorithmic/semantic tradeoffs, not an execution-resource inventory.
- **R3 — spilling:** Laurens Kuiper, Peter A. Boncz, Hannes Mühleisen. *Robust External Hash Aggregation in the Solid State Age*. ICDE 2024. [Official DuckDB publication page](https://duckdb.org/library/robust-external-hash-aggregation/), [official paper PDF](https://duckdb.org/pdf/ICDE2024-kuiper-boncz-muehleisen-out-of-core.pdf). Sections III–V describe unified temporary/persistent buffer management, spillable page layout, and parallel hash aggregation. The paper predates the pinned v2 API; its implementation/results do not establish current public custom-state hooks.
- **R4 — cardinality and skew:** Daniel Xue, Ryan Marcus. *Global Hash Tables Strike Back! An Analysis of Parallel GROUP BY Aggregation*. arXiv:2505.04153v2, 2025-09-05. [Versioned primary paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.04153v2), [versioned full text](https://arxiv.org/html/2505.04153v2). Sections 2–4 compare shared ticketing, update alternatives, partitioning, cardinality, skew, resizing, and memory complexity. Preprint status is explicit. Its ordinary SUM experiments are not checked-prefix/strict-f64 correctness evidence.
